third_party: small and almost entirely soft: numpy/tokenizers/transformers are all try-guarded, pytest is 100% confined to test files, and there is NO mlx or mlx_lm import anywhere -- MLX is driven by shelling out to a binary, not imported in process. prompt_toolkit is the only hard third-party import, and only for the REPL.

the_real_coupling.mechanism_2: sys.path hacks: hcli inserts tools/future onto sys.path then does bare `import organ_allocation`. Same coupling, disguised as a local import. 3 production sites plus ~15 in tests.
the_real_coupling.widest: tools.verify.status_causality, imported by all 8 agentos *_gate.py files

latent_bug_found: All 8 gates do `sc.emit = emit` -- assigning over a SHARED module's global. That is not sharing a utility, it is whichever gate ran last winning. No test exercises two gates in one process, so it is latent rather than observed. Flagged, not fixed: out of scope here and it deserves a real seam (an injected callback) rather than a quick patch.
the_one_clean_subsystem: backends.py. All four RuntimeBackend subclasses -- llama-server, mlx_lm.server, OpenAI-compatible HTTP, and the Rust native binary -- are wired through one classify_backend factory with live non-test callers. This is the only place in the pass where the campaign's usual registered-but-unreachable pattern did NOT appear, and all three required binaries are present on this host.
structural: hcli/paths.py defines repo root by the presence of tools/headless or crates -- sibling directories hcli does not own. hcli's notion of its own root depends on things outside it, which is what would block dropping it into another tree.

ABSORB: tools.accelerator.* (5 modules, all CLI command bodies living outside the CLI)
BOUND: tools.verify.status_causality (needs a seam before the monkeypatching is safe to depend on)
KEEP: the 4 runtime backends -- already correctly isolated behind an ABC
machine_genome.json -- a data contract, not a code import

my_own_defect_this_pass_found: The --model fix I landed an hour earlier had a residual gap. resolve_model() returns whatever _info_from_path gives, INCLUDING None, so a typo or a path relative to the caller's shell (the worker runs with cwd=workspace) silently yielded no model and deferred the failure into a backend. Worse, my regression test only grepped _spawn_worker's SOURCE for a string -- the same source-text testing I criticise elsewhere. Now validated at start_resident with a behavioural test and a negative control.
